facts.value: Quantitative psychological research lends itself to statistical hypothesis testing. Although the field makes abundant use of randomized and controlled experiments in laboratory settings, such research can only assess a limited range of short-term phenomena.
facts.programme_association: Psychology and Sociology - BA | University of Limerick

facts.value: Some psychologists rely on less rigorously controlled, but more ecologically valid field experiments.
facts.programme_association: Psychology and Sociology - BA | University of Limerick

facts.value: Research psychologists employ statistical methods to glean knowledge from population data, including the Pearson product–moment correlation coefficient, analysis of variance, multiple linear regression, logistic regression, structural equation modeling, and hierarchical linear modeling.
facts.programme_association: Psychology and Sociology - BA | University of Limerick

facts.value: The measurement and operationalization of important constructs are essential parts of these research designs.
facts.programme_association: Psychology and Sociology - BA | University of Limerick

facts.value: Some psychologists conduct qualitative research, which can involve interviews, questionnaires, and first-hand observation.
facts.programme_association: Psychology and Sociology - BA | University of Limerick

facts.value: While hypothesis testing is rare, virtually impossible, in qualitative research, qualitative studies can be helpful in theory and hypothesis generation, interpreting seemingly contradictory quantitative findings, and understanding why some interventions fail and others succeed.
facts.programme_association: Psychology and Sociology - BA | University of Limerick
